project.name: Inventory App
project.description:
Stock tracking for the warehouse team: accounts and sign-in, stock items, and stock movements.

Every endpoint follows these conventions:

- **Errors** are problem details ([RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457)) in `application/problem+json`; branch on `type`. 400 means invalid query or header parameters, 422 invalid body fields (listed in `errors`), and 404 an unknown or deleted ID. Other errors, like 415 or 500, are problem details too.
- **Authentication**: send `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. A 401 means the token is missing or expired: refresh once with `POST /auth/refresh`, then retry. If refreshing answers 401, sign in again.
- **Paged lists** return `{ data, meta }` and take `page` and `pageSize`. Short lists return `{ data }`.
- **Creates** take an `Idempotency-Key` header, so a retry never creates something twice.
- **Requests** send JSON. PATCH sends a JSON Merge Patch (`application/merge-patch+json`).
- **Responses** send `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- **CORS** allows only the app's origin, with credentials. It exposes `Location` and `Retry-After` to scripts, and allows the `Idempotency-Key` request header.
- **Times** are UTC, in RFC 3339 format.

endpoints.description: Returns an access token and sets the refresh token cookie. A session lasts 12 hours, or 30 days with `remember`, from sign-in; refreshing doesn't make it longer. Wrong credentials answer 400, not 401: a 401 always means the access token is missing or expired.

remember.description: Keep the session for 30 days instead of 12 hours

Set-Cookie.description: The refresh token. With `remember`, `Max-Age` keeps it for the session's 30 days; without, it's a browser-session cookie.
examples: refresh_token=rt_5Jx2mQ9vL0aR; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/v1/auth; Max-Age=2592000

Cache-Control.description: Tokens must never be stored by a cache (RFC 6749)

endpoints.notesFe: Keep the access token in memory, not in localStorage. Send API requests with `credentials: 'include'` so the browser keeps the cookie.
endpoints.notesBe: Answer 400 for unknown emails too, and hash the password for them as well, so neither the answer nor its timing shows who has an account. Answer 403 only once the password matched. Throttle failed attempts per email and per IP address, unknown emails included, instead of locking accounts: a lock would let anyone lock a colleague out.

endpoints.description: Always answers 202, whether or not the email has an account, so it doesn't show who has one. A new account gets a link to verify the address. An existing account gets an email saying so, with links to sign in and to reset the password; an unverified one gets a new link.

password.description: At least 12 characters, and not in known data breaches

errors.detail: This password appeared in a data breach. Choose another.

endpoints.notesBe: The verification link works for 24 hours. New accounts get the staff role; admins are promoted outside this app. Check passwords against known breached passwords (NIST SP 800-63B).

endpoints.description: The token comes from the link in the verification email: `/verify-email?token=…`. A link that was already used answers 204 again while its account stays verified, so opening it twice, or an email scanner opening it first, isn't an error.

errors.detail: Send the token from the link.

endpoints.description: Always answers 202, so it doesn't show which emails have accounts. An account that's already verified gets an email saying so, with a link to sign in; an unknown email gets nothing.
The link works once, for 1 hour. Always answers 202, so it doesn't show which emails have accounts.

The token comes from the link in the reset email: `/reset-password?token=…`. Ends every session of the user: refresh tokens stop working at once, and access tokens already issued expire within 15 minutes.

password.description: At least 12 characters, and not in known data breaches

errors.detail: This password appeared in a data breach. Choose another.

endpoints.notesBe: Store reset tokens hashed. Revoke every refresh token of the user.

endpoints.description: Exchanges the refresh token cookie for a new access token, and replaces the cookie. The session still ends 12 hours, or 30 days, after sign-in.

Set-Cookie.description: The new refresh token, with the same attributes. `Max-Age`, if set, is the time left in the session.
examples: refresh_token=rt_8Kd3nW1pZ7bT; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/v1/auth; Max-Age=2505600

Cache-Control.description: Tokens must never be stored by a cache (RFC 6749)

endpoints.notesFe: Call it directly, not through the code that refreshes on 401. Run one refresh at a time, across tabs too (e.g. with the Web Locks API): requests that get a 401 meanwhile wait for it, then retry once.
endpoints.notesBe: Rotate the refresh token on every use. Accept the previous token for 30 seconds after it's replaced, since tabs can refresh at the same moment; after that, a reused token was probably stolen, so revoke every session of the user. Only accept requests whose `Origin` is the app.

endpoints.description: Revokes the refresh token in the cookie, if there is one, and clears the cookie. Always answers 204, so signing out can't fail.

examples: refresh_token=; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/v1/auth; Max-Age=0

endpoints.notesFe: The access token works until it expires, so drop it from memory, even if this request fails.
endpoints.notesBe: Only revoke when the request's `Origin` is the app.

Idempotency-Key.description: A random value, like a UUID, for each thing to create. Resending with the same key gets the first success back (for 24 hours) instead of creating again. Failures aren't remembered, so a fixed request can reuse the key. The key with a different body after a success answers 400; a resend while the first request runs answers 409 `request-in-progress`.
